review_output: {"summary":"I found no privilege escalation or cross-vendor spoofing in this code. The trigger uses only static SQL, every table it touches is schema-qualified, and each scope is checked against Live.vendorId. Lock order is generation → version → report, and readers take no locks, so I found no lifecycle-vs-payment deadlock cycle. Payment writes are not cleared for release: every Serializable payment on the same live updates one shared row, so concurrent writes on that row fail with 40001. That pressure is untested, and the existing retries may not absorb it. Also, nothing here shows the metric worker's runtime role can access the generation table. Other issues are minor.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Availability/payment","file":"20261015140000_live_metric_order_source/migration.sql","issue":"Every payment or order write for one live updates the same LiveMetricOrderSource row inside a Serializable transaction.","evidence":"ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET revision=source.revision+1. Check 2 shows the stale writer gets 40001. Claim and finish hold FOR SHARE on this row. The webhook retries only twice.","impact":"During a burst of sales on a popular live, concurrent payment webhooks can fail with 40001 or lock timeouts and run out of retries. Metric invalidation would then decide whether payment status persists.","recommended_fix":"Remove the hot row from the payment path: use an append-only change log or outbox processed after commit, or a per-scope sharded counter. A spurious invalidation is safe. Alternatively, catch the failure so the metric write can never fail the payment.","required_test":"N concurrent Serializable payments on one live (N≥20) plus a claim/finish loop. Every payment must eventually commit and the report must end up not current.","confidence":0.75},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Privileges","file":"both migrations, live-metric-report-reader.ts","issue":"The generation table has RLS enabled, no policies and no grants. The create, claim and finish functions, the guard trigger and the readers all run as the caller (SECURITY INVOKER).","evidence":"REVOKE ALL on the table plus ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The functions INSERT into and SELECT ... FOR SHARE from the table, and reportSnapshot runs a subquery against it.","impact":"Unless the worker connects as the table owner, the lifecycle fails with 42501 and readers see NULL, so every report shows as unavailable. If the worker does connect as owner, RLS has no effect.","recommended_fix":"Grant the worker role exactly SELECT and INSERT with a policy, or make the lifecycle functions SECURITY DEFINER with pinned search_path. Document the worker role.","required_test":"Use a NOLOGIN worker role with only its intended grants. Create, claim, finish and read must all succeed, and direct access to the generation table must be denied.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Deadlock","file":"20261015140000_live_metric_order_source/migration.sql","issue":"Scopes are sorted within one row-trigger call but not across rows or statements in a transaction.","evidence":"T1 updates an order on live A, then a payment on live B. T2 does B, then A. Bulk UPDATE statements touch rows in arbitrary order.","impact":"Deadlock (40P01). Prisma maps this to P2034, but the raw SQL path is only tested for 40001.","recommended_fix":"Treat 40P01 as retryable in the raw SQL paths. Process bulk writes in sorted order or invalidate once per statement.","required_test":"Two transactions touch lives in opposite order. Expect 40P01, a retry, and correct final revisions.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Trigger attachment","file":"20261015140000_live_metric_order_source/migration.sql","issue":"The function branches on TG_TABLE_NAME only and treats every other table as PaymentTransaction.","evidence":"There is no check of TG_TABLE_SCHEMA or TG_RELID.","impact":"Anyone holding EXECUTE (the owner or a later accidental grant) can attach it to any table with a metadata column and force invalidations for any live of a vendor.","recommended_fix":"RAISE unless TG_RELID is CommerceOrder's or PaymentTransaction's regclass and TG_LEVEL is ROW. Use search_path=pg_catalog only.","required_test":"Attaching the function to a table named public.\"CommerceOrder\" in another schema, or to any other table, must raise an error.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Missed invalidation","file":"20261015140000_live_metric_order_source/migration.sql","issue":"TRUNCATE, and writes made with triggers disabled (session_replication_role=replica), skip invalidation.","evidence":"Only AFTER ... FOR EACH ROW triggers on INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE are defined.","impact":"A ready report stays current after admin, restore or replication data changes.","recommended_fix":"Add an AFTER TRUNCATE statement trigger that bumps or deletes every scope. Document that restores must bump generations.","required_test":"After TRUNCATE CommerceOrder, readMetricReadyReport returns unavailable.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Spoofed lifecycle","file":"20261015150000_live_metric_order_report_binding/migration.sql","issue":"The wp20.report_writer setting gates writes but grants no privilege. Any role with UPDATE on the report table can call set_config('wp20.report_writer','finish') and mark a report ready with any result.","evidence":"The guard checks the setting and the revisions but not leaseOwner or lease expiry.","impact":"Report results can be forged by anyone with direct table access. This is acceptable only if the tables stay owner-only.","recommended_fix":"Keep table rights revoked. Move all writes into SECURITY DEFINER functions and also check the lease in the guard.","required_test":"A role with UPDATE that sets the GUC and writes ready without a lease must be rejected.","confidence":0.5}]}
